authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.
authoredInteractions: - equation_input for the two lower boundary equations: two fields pre-filled with "-x + 1" (left, for R1) and "x + 1" (right, for R2); when the learner edits either, the corresponding boundary line redraws, the shaded sub-regions R1 and R2 update, and the inner integral limits display — shows directly how the lower boundary formula changing expression at x=0 is what forces the decomposition into two sub-integrals
authoredContext:
Evaluate !! R (2x − y2 ) dA over the triangular region R enclosed between the lines y =−x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3.  In Example 4 we could have treated R as a type I region, but with an added complication.
Viewed as a type I region, the upper boundary of R is the line y = 3 (Figure 14.2.9) and
the lower boundary consists of two parts, the line y =−x + 1 to the left of the y-axis and

discrepancies: Right sub-region R2 is filled a tan/orange (#fbe3b6) rather than the pale cream-yellow the source uses, slightly muting the blue/yellow contrast
Boundary equation labels use an ASCII hyphen-minus ('y = -x + 1') instead of the proper minus glyph ('y = −x + 1') shown in the source
R1 and R2 are drawn as a separate italic 'R' plus an offset digit rather than true subscripts, so the subscript sits a touch low and detached
An integrand (2x − y²) and a numeric double-integral readout are added in the side panel; the source figure shows only the region decomposition with no integrand
evaluation.notes: The triangle geometry, piecewise boundaries, R1/R2 split, red vertical strips, axes and ticks all match the source closely, and unlike a naive port the equation inputs are genuinely wired (setFn/setLower plus root-finding redraw the lines, fills and limits) with a working 4-step highlight player; weaknesses are minor color/glyph/subscript styling and an invented integrand readout not present in the source.
action_items: Replace the ASCII hyphen in the boundary labels with a true minus glyph (−) to match the source typography.
Render R1/R2 as real subscripts (e.g. tspan/baseline-shift or a single text with dy) so the digit aligns cleanly under the R instead of floating as separate offset text.
Lighten the R2 fill toward the source's pale cream-yellow (e.g. #fdeec9) to restore the intended blue/yellow distinction.
Either remove the fabricated 2x − y² integrand or explicitly caption the readout as an 'example integrand' so students do not think the source figure specifies one.
